era: 1894 年 11 月 27 日生于和歌山县海草郡和佐村一个没落地主家庭，幼名幸吉——家中八个孩子他最小，父亲做米投机失败破产，1901 年举家迁和歌山市开木屐店，两年后店歇业，1904 年 9 岁的松下独身到大阪当学徒：先在宫田火盆店看孩子磨火盆，后到五代自行车店当学徒五年——学会的是殷勤待客、商品陈列与'舍不得慢待一位客人'的商人本能——1910 年 15 岁转入大阪电灯股份公司，从见习配线工做到检查员，其间自学夜校未果却读遍肯德基《自助论》，1917 年 22 岁因自行改良的电灯插座不被公司采纳而辞职，与妻子梅乃、内弟井植岁男在大阪猪饲野的出租屋里创立'松下电器具制作所'，资本仅 97 日元 20 钱——第一个产品插座无人问津，靠接活陶瓷绝缘器的订单救急；1918 年改良的自行车炮弹形车灯以'点三十小时以上'的宣传和 30 个免费样品店头试点的打法打开市场，'National'品牌同年注册——1923 年发明的电池灯与 1927 年 square 电热器、超级电熨斗把'大规模生产廉价好物'的路子走通——1929 年世界经济危机中库存积压一半，他病中做出'生产额减半、只做半天工、全体员工转为销售库存、工资一分不减'的决定，两个月库存卖尽——1933 年首创事业部制（收音机/电灯电池/配电线具三部门各负盈亏），1935 年改组为股份公司；战时受军需裹挟扩产造船飞机，战后被驻日盟军指定为财阀整肃对象（A 级），经工会与经销商 1.5 万人联名请愿免职除名——1950 年代重整旗鼓，1952 年与飞利浦合资引进电子技术，1955 年后电视、洗衣机、冰箱'三种神器'进入日本家庭；1959 年成立美国松下，把'自来水哲学'推向海外——1961 年 66 岁辞社长任会长，把经营交给山下俊彦一代的职业经理人体系——1946 年创立 PHP 研究所（Peace and Happiness through Prosperity），1979 年以 84 岁高龄创办松下政经塾培养政经人才，晚年捐巨资设松下社会科学振兴财团——1989 年 4 月 27 日以 94 岁去世，被称为'经营之神'；留下的不是一家公司，而是一套'企业是公器'的经营哲学。
era_en: Born 27 November 1894 in Wasa village, Wakayama, to a declining landowning family, youngest of eight — his father lost everything speculating in rice, the family moved to Wakayama city to run a wooden-clog shop that closed within two years, and in 1904, at nine, Matsushita was sent alone to Osaka as an apprentice: first minding children and polishing hibachi at the Miyata brazier shop, then five years at the Godai bicycle shop — where he absorbed the merchant instincts of courteous service, merchandise display and never slighting a single customer — in 1910, at fifteen, he joined Osaka Electric Light as an apprentice wiring man, rising to inspector, teaching himself nights (without finishing night school) and reading Self-Help through; in 1917, at twenty-two, his improved lamp socket rejected by the company, he resigned and founded 'Matsushita Electric Device Works' in a rented room at Ikaino, Osaka, with his wife Mumeno and brother-in-law Toshio Iue, capital 97 yen 20 sen — the first socket sold nothing and order work for insulator plates kept the shop alive; the 1918 bullet-shaped bicycle lamp, promoted as 'lighting thirty hours or more' and seeded through thirty shops with free samples that left their batteries flat, opened the market, and the 'National' brand was registered the same year — the 1923 bullet lamp, the 1927 square heater and Super Iron made 'mass-produce good things cheaply' a working formula — in the 1929 depression, with stock piled to half of production, he ordered from his sickbed: production halved, half-day work only, every employee rotated onto selling the inventory, wages untouched; the stock was gone in two months — in 1933 he invented the divisional system (radio, lamp-battery, wiring, each with its own profit and loss), reorganising as a joint-stock company in 1935; wartime military demand dragged him into shipbuilding and aircraft, and after defeat the Occupation designated him a Class-A zaibatsu to be purged — a petition of 15,000 union members and dealers saved his chair — through the 1950s he rebuilt: the 1952 joint venture with Philips imported electronics technology, and televisions, washing machines and refrigerators, the 'three sacred treasures', entered Japanese homes; Matsushita Electric of America followed in 1959, carrying the tap-water philosophy abroad — in 1961, at sixty-six, he stepped down to chairman, handing operations to professional managers of the Yamashita generation — in 1946 he founded the PHP Institute (Peace and Happiness through Prosperity), in 1979, at eighty-four, the Matsushita School of Government and Economics to train public talent, and endowed the Matsushita Foundation for social sciences — he died 27 April 1989 at ninety-four, called the 'god of management'; what he left was not one company but a philosophy: the enterprise is a public instrument of society.
school: 企业经营哲学 / 大众消费品工业 / 组织与人事管理 / 商业伦理（企业公器论）/ 教育与公益
historical_significance: 把'让好东西像自来水一样多而便宜'从一句理想做成二十世纪的产业方法：他从 97 日元起家，以炮弹车灯、超级电熨斗、三种神器把电器从奢侈品变成日用品，把日本家庭拉进电气时代；他在经营制度上的发明同样深刻——事业部制（1933）先于通用汽车的风格在日本生根，水库式经营、玻璃式经营、按需求定价（价定后逼成本）成为战后日本式经营的通用语法；1929 年'不裁员、减半生产、全员卖库存'与 1964 年热海会议'三天只听不说'，示范了危机中的雇主伦理与倾听式经营；他 66 岁交棒、84 岁办学，晚年以 PHP 与政经塾把利润转写为公共哲学——被称为'经营之神'，但真正传世的是他反复申明的那句话：企业是社会的公器，利润是它对社会尽责的凭证。
historical_significance_en: He turned the ideal 'make good things as plentiful and cheap as tap water' into an industrial method of the twentieth century: starting from 97 yen, with the bullet bicycle lamp, the Super Iron and the three sacred treasures he turned electric goods from luxuries into daily necessities and pulled Japanese households into the electric age; his institutional inventions ran as deep — the divisional system (1933) took root in Japan ahead of its GM-style fashion, and dam management, glass-wall management and demand-first pricing (set the price, then force the cost) became the common grammar of post-war Japanese management; the 1929 decision 'no layoffs, halve production, all hands sell stock' and the 1964 Atami conference 'three days of listening, no defence' modelled employer ethics and listening management in crisis; retiring at sixty-six and founding a school at eighty-four, in his last decades he converted profit into public philosophy through PHP and the Matsushita School — called the 'god of management', yet what endures is his repeated declaration: the enterprise is society's public instrument, and profit is the receipt of its service.
unique_thinking: 松下的思维内核是'先问这件东西对社会有什么用，再问怎么把它变得又多又便宜'——自来水哲学不是营销口号，而是把使命放在定价之前的顺序：贵到只有少数人用得起，就不是好产品；第二个内核是'素直之心'——不带成见地先听清事实再判断，热海会议上他对经销商的抱怨三天的反应不是辩解而是'请继续讲'，因为他相信真相只在对方把话说完之后才出现；他对得失有一套'塞翁'式的账法：1932 年他宣布事业的目的不是松下的利润而是'逐步提高人类生活的品质'，1929 年的危机在他账上不是灾难而是'把全员变成销售员的机会'；他坚信经营需要'水库'——设备、资金、库存、心态都要留余量，景气时蓄水，萧条时放水；他要求账本透明到每个员工看得见，'玻璃式经营'使猜疑无处生长；他把事业部做成'社中之社'，让独当一面的经营者自己背盈亏；他对价格的理解是反常识的：价格由消费者决定，成本是价格定了以后逼出来的管理对象；他 66 岁交出经营权——不是退休而是把公司交给制度而非人；84 岁办学立塾，把'企业是公器'写成留给下一代的功课。
unique_thinking_en: Matsushita's cognitive core is to ask first what a thing does for society, then how to make it plentiful and cheap — the tap-water philosophy is not a slogan but an ordering: mission before price; a good too expensive for ordinary people is not yet a product. His second core is the 'unbiased mind' — hear the facts fully before judging; at the Atami conference his response to three days of dealers' grievances was not defence but 'please go on', because he believed truth appears only after the other side finishes speaking. He kept a Saigyō-style ledger of gain and loss: in 1932 he declared the purpose of the enterprise to be not Matsushita's profit but 'steadily raising the quality of human life', and the 1929 crisis entered his books not as disaster but as 'the chance to make every employee a salesperson'. He held that management needs dams — capacity, cash, inventory, even mentality, must hold slack, hoarded in boom, released in bust. He demanded accounts transparent enough for every employee to read — glass-wall management, leaving suspicion nowhere to grow. He built divisions as companies within the company, each head carrying his own profit and loss. His view of price defies convention: the customer sets the price, and cost is the object managed after the price is fixed. At sixty-six he handed over operations — not retiring but subordinating the company to institutions rather than persons; at eighty-four he founded a school, leaving 'the enterprise is a public instrument' as homework for the next generation.
civilization_zh: 明治-昭和日本：纪州藩士没落之后的大阪学徒传统、关西'服务至上'的商人伦理（石田梅岩'石门心学'的市井余脉）、大正-昭和电气化大众消费的黎明、战后财阀解体与金库（系列）企业群的崛起、儒家'教养主义'与神道'产业报国'精神在公司伦理中的合流
civilization_en: Meiji-Shōwa Japan: the Osaka apprenticeship tradition rising from a fallen Kishū samurai line, the Kansai merchant ethics of service (the marketplace afterglow of Ishida Baigan's Shingaku), the dawn of electrified mass consumption in Taishō-Shōwa, the post-war dissolution of the zaibatsu and the rise of keiretsu groups, and the confluence of Confucian 'cultivation' and Shinto 'industrial service to the nation' inside corporate ethics
roles_zh: 企业家与发明经营者（松下电器创始人）；事业部制与水库式经营的创立者；经营哲学家（PHP 研究所创办人）；教育家（松下政经塾创办人）；雇主伦理的示范者
roles_en: Entrepreneur and inventive manager (founder of Matsushita Electric); creator of the divisional system and dam management; philosopher of management (founder of the PHP Institute); educator (founder of the Matsushita School of Government and Economics); exemplar of employer ethics
key_works: 《自来水哲学》(1932 年创业使命宣言；晚年同名自传)——企业使命与量产廉价哲学的源头文本
《经营须知· contrasting 十二条》与《工作·生活·思考》——经营哲学的系统表述

modes.domain_zh: 商业方法论/以'让必需品像自来水一样多而便宜'为使命决定产品与定价的先后顺序
modes.domain_en: Business methodology / taking 'make necessities as plentiful and cheap as tap water' as the mission that orders product and price
modes.definition_zh: 企业使命方法论/把'社会需要什么'置于'企业能赚什么'之前，并以量产把价格压到人人可及：松下对自来水怀有近乎宗教的感慨——路边的自来水没人抱怨被喝了，因为充足且便宜；他把这个意象立为松下电器的使命（1932 年'知命'之年宣言）：'让电器像自来水一样无限供应，尽属我界'——使命先行带来三个经营推论：产品只做大众的必需品（灯、熨斗、收音机，而非贵族玩具）；定价按'普通家庭用得起'倒推，而不是按成本加成；产能与销量以普及率为标尺——'产业人的使命在于克服贫困，把生活水准提到丰裕的高度'；使命不是道德装饰，是排序规则：当利润与普及冲突时，普及优先
modes.definition_en: Corporate-mission methodology: place 'what does society need' before 'what can the firm earn', and use mass production to price within everyone's reach: Matsushita felt an almost religious gratitude before tap water — no one scolds you for drinking from a public fountain, because it is abundant and nearly free; he made the image Matsushita Electric's mission (declared in 1932, his 'knowing the mandate' year): 'make electric goods as inexhaustible as tap water, and bring them within everyone's reach'; the mission-first order yields three corollaries: make only the masses' necessities (lamps, irons, radios — not aristocrats' toys); set price by what an ordinary household can pay, then manage cost backwards; measure capacity and sales by penetration rate — 'the industrialist's mission is to overcome poverty and raise the standard of living to plenty'; the mission is not moral ornament but an ordering rule: when profit and penetration conflict, penetration wins
modes.source_chapter: 松下幸之助 1932 年创业使命宣言（'知命'演说）；《自来水哲学》自传第 4-5 章
modes.key_quote_zh: 路边的水龙头白给水喝也没人抱怨——我的事业就是让电器也流成这样的自来水：无限供应，人人可用。
modes.key_quote_en: No one complains about drinking free from the public fountain — my business is to make electric goods flow like that water: inexhaustible, and within everyone's reach.
key_concepts: 使命先行 mission first（先定社会用途，再谈利润——价格跟着使命走）
普及率标尺 penetration yardstick（以'多少家庭用上了'而非'毛利率'衡量业绩）
必需品清单 the necessity list（灯、熨斗、收音机——只做大众生活里排得上号的东西）
process_zh: 把行业产物翻译成'生活必需或非必需'：问这件东西在普通家庭的账本里排第几位——松下只做排得进前几十位的品类
按'用得起'定目标价而非按成本定售价：先问普通家庭肯为它付多少，再设计成本与工艺去够这个价
以量产与通用件把价格推向目标：标准化、大批量、自建渠道——让销量自己把成本压下去
以普及率为最高业绩指标：市场份额是手段，'多少家庭的生活因它改善'才是完成态
process_en: Translate the industry's output into 'necessity or not': ask where the product ranks in an ordinary household's ledger — Matsushita made only items that ranked in the top few dozen
Set a target price by affordability, not cost: ask first what an ordinary family would pay, then design process and cost to meet it
Push the price toward the target with volume and standard parts: standardise, mass-produce, build your own channel — let sales volume grind the cost down
Take penetration as the top metric: market share is the means; 'how many households live better because of it' is the finished state
representative_cases_zh: 炮弹形自行车灯 (1923)：把夜路照明从'用蜡烛的临时办法'变成'换电池的日用品'——先以 30 家店免费样品让店头亮起来，再以低定价走量，最终成为骑车人的标准配置
超级电熨斗与 square 电热器 (1927)：以'普通主妇买得起'定价倒推设计，电熨斗从奢侈品变成家家有一件
三种神器 (1950 年代)：电视、洗衣机、冰箱按'何时进普通家庭'倒排产品计划——1950-60 年代日本家庭电器普及率的曲线，就是这条使命的账本
representative_cases_en: The bullet bicycle lamp (1923): turning night-road lighting from a candle stopgap into a battery-changed daily good — first thirty shops lit by free samples, then volume at a low price, until it became the cyclist's standard kit
The Super Iron and square heater (1927): priced by 'what an ordinary housewife can pay' with design forced backward from the price — the iron ceased to be a luxury and became a household item

The three sacred treasures (1950s): televisions, washing machines, refrigerators planned backwards from 'when they enter ordinary homes' — Japan's 1950s-60s appliance penetration curve is this mission's ledger
modern_applications_zh: 科技公司使命校准：'让 X 像自来水一样'检验——你的产品是给前 1% 的玩具，还是给所有人的日用品
下沉市场策略：先定'这批人付得起的价格'再设计产品（小米、拼多多、传音的定价倒推法）
ESG 落地：把'改善多少人生活'写进 KPI 顶层而非年报附录——使命变成排序规则而非宣传页
modern_applications_en: Mission calibration for tech: the tap-water test — is your product a toy for the top 1% or a daily good for everyone
Mass-market strategy: fix the price the target population can pay, then design the product (Xiaomi, Pinduoduo, Transsion's backward pricing)
ESG that bites: write 'how many lives improved' into top-line KPIs, not the annual report's appendix — mission as ordering rule, not brochure

modes.domain_zh: 认识论/先悬置成见听清事实再作判断的心智纪律
modes.domain_en: Epistemology / the mental discipline of suspending preconception until the facts are fully heard
modes.definition_zh: 认识论方法论/判断之前先做两件事：把事实听到说完，把自己想赢的欲望放一放——松下称之为'素直之心'（すなお）：不受私心、成见、恐惧和面子扭曲的原始心智，'像一面擦净的镜子照见事物本相'；它的操作形态是先听后判：1964 年热海会议上，面对 200 多家代理店连珠炮似的抱怨（'松下压货''价格没人管''返点太抠'），松下听完两天多的控诉只说'我明白了，请继续讲'，第三天才开口，开口第一句是'诸位说的都是对的'——素直之心不是没有立场，而是让立场最后上场：先让事实说话，判断在事实说完之后才被允许成形
modes.definition_en: Epistemological methodology: before judging, do two things — hear the facts to their end, and set aside your wish to win — what Matsushita called the 'unbiased mind' (sunao): the original mentality undistorted by self-interest, prejudice, fear or face, 'a mirror wiped clean, showing things as they are'; its operational form is listen-first, judge-last: at the 1964 Atami conference, facing hours of gripe from 200-plus distributors ('Matsushita forces stock on us', 'nobody police the prices', 'the rebates are stingy'), he listened for two days saying only 'I understand; please go on'; he spoke on the third day, and his first sentence was 'everything you say is right'; the unbiased mind is not having no position but letting the position enter last: facts speak first, and judgment is permitted to form only after the facts have finished
modes.source_chapter: 松下幸之助《素直之心》(PHP 研究所)；热海会议 (1964 年 7 月，王子饭店) 参加者回忆录
modes.key_quote_zh: 诸位说的都是对的——这话不是客气话：我不听完就不配说任何话。
modes.key_quote_en: 'Everything you say is right' — and it was no courtesy: until I have heard it to the end, I have not earned a single remark.
key_concepts: 素直之心 sunao（不受私心与面子扭曲的镜子心智）
先听后判 listen first, judge last（判断在事实说完之后才被允许上场）
忘我倾听 selfless listening（把'想辩解的我'暂时请出房间）
process_zh: 把'待判事项'先冻结：宣布'今天只听不说'——给倾听设定不受打断的边界（热海第一天不开口）
记录而不反驳：把对方的每条指控原样记下，不给'但是'——反驳欲望出现时标记它而非执行它
听完之后复述确认：用对方的话把问题重述一遍请其确认——确保听到的是对方的账而非自己的版本
事实说完后才下判断，且先承认对方对的部分：'诸位说的都是对的'，再谈自己能改什么
process_en: Freeze the matter to be judged: declare 'today we only listen' — fence the listening from interruption (Atami day one: silence)
Record without rebutting: take down each charge verbatim, no 'but' — when the urge to defend appears, tag it, don't act on it
After hearing, restate for confirmation: repeat the problem in the speaker's own words and ask if it is right — make sure you heard their ledger, not your version
Judge only after the facts finish, and concede what is right first: 'everything you say is right', then discuss what you can change
representative_cases_zh: 热海会议 (1964)：代理店积怨总爆发，松下听两天说一天，会议以'全面改革销售体制'收场——信任崩塌被一场倾听止住，此后十年松下渠道反而更紧
'闷专答'故事：他年轻时答不出的问题不装懂，记下来回去想——'不懂装懂是素直之心的头号敌人'
PHP 研究所的研究方法：立题先列'我希望它成立什么'，再逐条找反例——研究所以'素直'为社训训练研究员先破自己的期望
representative_cases_en: The Atami conference (1964): distributors' pent grievances detonated; Matsushita listened two days, spoke one, and the meeting closed with a full reform of the sales system — a collapse of trust stopped by listening, and the channel grew tighter for a decade after
The 'silent about what I don't know' habit: young Matsushita would not bluff an answer — he wrote it down and went off to think; 'pretending to know is the unbiased mind's first enemy'
PHP research method: state the thesis with its hoped conclusion listed first, then hunt counterexamples one by one — the institute trains researchers to break their own hopes under the banner 'sunao'
modern_applications_zh: 客户访谈/用户研究：先冻结产品方案再做访谈——'只听不说'的一号纪律，反驳欲出现先标记
组织复盘：事故复盘先让一线讲完再让管理层说话——'复盘会第一句话永远是请继续'
谈判：先复述对方立场并获确认再出价——素直之心是最便宜的谈判武器
modern_applications_en: Customer interviews and user research: freeze the product plan before interviewing — rule one, listen only; tag the urge to defend
Organisational post-mortems: frontline speaks to the end before management — the first sentence of a retro is always 'please go on'
Negotiation: restate the other side's position and win confirmation before quoting a price — the unbiased mind is the cheapest negotiation weapon there is

埃德加·沙因（潜在：'谦逊探询'的组织心理学者后裔）

modes.domain_zh: 方法论/把灾难改记为另一种资产账目并当场给出兑现动作
modes.domain_en: Methodology / re-entering a disaster in the books as another kind of asset and naming the action that cashes it
modes.definition_zh: 经营韧性方法论/坏事件发生时不按'损失账'记账，而按'转化机会账'重记，并立刻给出把机会兑现的机制：1929 年大萧条，松下电器库存积压达产量一半、销量腰斩，行业标准动作是裁员一半；松下病中给井植与武久下的指令是：'生产减半，工厂只做半天工，员工一个不裁、工资全额照发——把人手全部转去销售库存'；两个月库存清空，'不裁员'反而成为松下此后数十年劳资信任的本金；他的账法来自'塞翁失马'的东方叙事：福祸相倚不是安慰，是要找到祸事里被锁进来的那份新资产（此处是：一支被证明与企业共存亡、且个个会卖货的员工队伍），并为它设计兑现动作（全员销售），否则'乐观'只是自我安慰
modes.definition_en: Resilience methodology: when bad events strike, do not book them as losses — re-enter them as assets of another kind, and at once design the mechanism that cashes them: in the 1929 depression, with stock piled to half of output and sales halved, the industry's standard move was to lay off half the workforce; Matsushita, from his sickbed, ordered Iue and Murai: 'halve production, work half days, cut not one employee and pay full wages — turn every pair of hands onto selling the stock'; the inventory cleared in two months, and 'no layoffs' became the principal of decades of labour trust at Matsushita; his ledger comes from the East Asian tale of the old man who lost his horse: fortune and misfortune lean on each other not as consolation but as bookkeeping — find the asset the disaster locked in (here: a workforce proven to share the firm's fate and able to sell), and design the action that redeems it (all-hands selling); without the action, 'optimism' is only self-soothing
modes.source_chapter: 1929 年'不裁员'决策记录（井植岁男、武久逸郎回忆）；《自来水哲学》'昭和恐慌'章
modes.key_quote_zh: 生产减半，工资分文不减，人手全部去卖库存——这次危机是让全公司变成销售部的天赐机会。
modes.key_quote_en: Halve production, cut not one yen of wages, put every pair of hands on selling the stock — this crisis is heaven's gift: the whole company becomes the sales department.
key_concepts: 重记账目 re-entry（坏事件不改性质，改记入哪本账）
被锁资产 the locked asset（灾难里被冻结的隐性资产：信任、人手、经验、渠道）
兑现机制 the redemption mechanism（没有具体动作的乐观是安慰，有动作的乐观是策略）
process_zh: 把灾难事件从'损失账'拿出来：先问这次事件里什么东西被'锁'住了（人手、信任、渠道、注意力）
给被锁资产重新标价：'全员卖库存'的价值不是省下裁员费，是买下一支共存亡的队伍——估它萧条之后的长期价值
设计兑现动作并当场公布：具体的、可执行的、与被锁资产一一对应的动作（生产减半+半天工+全员销售+工资全额）
把兑现过程记录进组织记忆：'1929 不裁员'成为松下劳资叙事的原点——下次危机时这笔账再次复利
process_en: Take the disaster out of the loss ledger: ask first what has been 'locked in' by the event — hands, trust, channels, attention
Re-price the locked asset: 'all hands sell stock' is worth not the layoff savings but a workforce that shares the firm's fate — value it by its post-slump long worth
Design the redemption action and announce it at once: concrete, executable, matched one-to-one to the locked asset (halve output, half days, all-hands selling, full wages)
Enter the redemption in organisational memory: 'no layoffs in 1929' became the origin of Matsushita's labour narrative — compounding again at the next crisis
representative_cases_zh: 1929 年不裁员决策：库存积压一半的危机被改记为'全员销售演习'——两个月清库存，松下成为'终身雇用'叙事的标志企业之一
战后被整肃 (1945-1947)：财阀指定、社长解职的至暗时刻，他以 1.5 万工会会员与经销商联名请愿保住职位——把'下台危机'改记为'检验劳资信任的实验'
晚年多病：年轻时肺病缠身被迫长期疗养，他自嘲'病弱给了我思考的时间'——PHP 与经营写作大半产于病榻，'体弱'被记成'哲学产出'的资产
representative_cases_en: The 1929 no-layoff decision: a crisis of stock at half of production re-entered as an all-hands sales exercise — inventory cleared in two months, and Matsushita became a flagship of the lifetime-employment narrative

The post-war purge (1945-47): Class-A zaibatsu designation and removal from the presidency; a petition of 15,000 union members and dealers restored him — a downfall crisis re-entered as a live test of labour trust

Sickness in youth: tuberculosis forced long sanatorium years; he joked that 'weakness gave me time to think' — much of PHP and his management writing was produced from the sickbed, frailty booked as an asset of philosophy
modern_applications_zh: 企业危机公关：裁员潮中'共享损失'方案（减薪+轮岗+转岗培训）对'一刀切裁员'的长期信任价差
个人挫折复盘：把被裁/落榜/项目失败改记为'被锁资产'（时间、技能、教训）并设计兑现动作
产品召回危机：把召回改记为'质量信任的预付'——主动召回企业的长期复购率显著高于被动应对者
modern_applications_en: Crisis PR for firms: shared-pain schemes (pay cuts, rotation, retraining) versus blanket layoffs — the long-run trust spread
Personal setback retros: re-enter being fired, failing an exam, a dead project as locked assets (time, skills, lessons) and design the redemption action
Product recalls: book the recall as prepayment on quality trust — firms that recall voluntarily show markedly higher long-run repurchase

modes.domain_zh: 商业方法论/在设备、资金、库存、心态上系统性留余量以穿越周期
modes.domain_en: Business methodology / systematically holding slack in capacity, cash, inventory and mindset to ride the cycle
modes.definition_zh: 经营周期方法论/把'留余量'从道德美德升级为经营制度：松下以水库为喻——河水丰时水库蓄水，涸时放水，'经营也当如此，景气时蓄（资金、设备、心态的余量），萧条时放'；其操作要点是把余量写进制度而非靠自律：设备不按峰值订单建（留 20-30% 弹性）、资金保持远超银行要求的自存比例、不追求满负荷运转、'雨天修屋顶'——好年景做坏年景的准备；最深刻的一条是'心态的水库'：经营者自己先不能被萧条吓垮，'没有水库是因为不想建'——余量首先是经营者的意志问题；与精益'零库存'相反，他赌的是周期的必然性：景气只是贷款，萧条才是还账
modes.definition_en: Business-cycle methodology: elevate 'holding slack' from private virtue to corporate institution: Matsushita's image is the dam — when the river is full the reservoir stores, when dry it releases, 'and so should management: in boom, store slack of cash, capacity and nerve; in bust, release it'; the operating point is writing slack into rules rather than relying on self-discipline: build capacity below peak orders (20-30% elastic headroom), hold cash far beyond what banks require, refuse full-load running, 'mend the roof in sunshine' — prepare for bad years in good ones; and deepest is the dam of the mind: the manager himself must not be panicked by the slump — 'there is no dam because you did not want one'; slack is first of all a matter of the manager's will; against lean 'zero inventory' he bets on the necessity of the cycle: boom is a loan, bust is the repayment
modes.source_chapter: 松下幸之助'水库式经营'讲演 (1960 年代巡回讲演系列)；《经营心得十二箇条》
modes.key_quote_zh: 天不下雨河就干了，可修了水库就有水——经营上没有水库，是因为你根本没打算修。
modes.key_quote_en: When no rain falls the river dries — but build a dam and there is water; if your management has no dam, it is because you never meant to build one.
key_concepts: 制度性余量 institutional slack（余量写进规章与预算线，不靠自觉）
心态水库 the mental dam（经营者的镇定是第一种余量——先于资金与设备）
雨天修屋顶 mending the roof in sunshine（好年景做坏年景的工程）
process_zh: 盘点四类水库：资金（现金/授信）、设备（产能弹性）、库存（安全水位）、心态（管理层的时间与镇定）——逐一设定目标水位
把水位写进制度：设备投资上限、现金保有红线、不接超产能订单的规则——余量由预算委员会守卫而非老板个人
景气期主动蓄水：把超额利润按比例存入'萧条准备'科目而非全部分红扩张
萧条期按预案放水：动用储备做研发、培训、渠道深耕——萧条不是收缩期，是用蓄水换份额的窗口
process_en: Inventory the four dams: cash (liquidity/credit lines), capacity (elastic headroom), inventory (safety level), nerve (management's time and calm) — set a target level for each
Write the levels into rules: caps on equipment spending, a red line for cash reserves, a rule against orders beyond capacity — slack guarded by the budget committee, not the boss's mood
Store deliberately in boom: bank excess profit into a 'slump reserve' line instead of paying it all out and expanding
Release by plan in bust: draw the reserve for R&D, training, channel deepening — the slump is not a contraction but the window in which stored water buys share
representative_cases_zh: 松下电器的'萧条准备金'：战后至 1960 年代公司账上长期保有远超同业的现金与有价证券——石油危机 (1973) 与广场协议 (1985) 两次外部冲击中，松下系是裁员最少、转型最早的日本大企业群之一
'只做半天工' (1929)：留余量制度的反向应用——用'生产减半+工资全额'的支出余量换'全员销售'的组织动员
1961 年交棒时的制度设计：社长卸任但保留会长职位与企业哲学的'水位计'角色——把'心态水库'制度化为会长对经营节奏的最后否决
representative_cases_en: Matsushita Electric's slump reserve: from the post-war years through the 1960s the company carried cash and securities far beyond its peers' — in the two external shocks of the oil crisis (1973) and the Plaza Accord (1985) the Matsushita group laid off least and pivoted earliest among Japan's giants
'Half-day work' (1929): the dam run in reverse — spending slack (halved output, full wages) exchanged for organisational mobilisation (all-hands selling)

The institutional design of the 1961 handover: the president steps down but the chairman keeps the post as gauge of the firm's philosophical water level — the mental dam institutionalised as the chairman's final veto on tempo
modern_applications_zh: 公司财务政策：设定'18 个月运营成本'现金红线并写进章程——余量不因牛市被股东压力侵蚀
个人生活设计：收入 40% 以下才有资格加杠杆——家庭版的水库式经营
科技公司产能规划：AI 算力/芯片备货留 30% 弹性——'缺芯潮'中水库型企业的份额暴涨
modern_applications_en: Corporate finance policy: a charter red line of 18 months' operating cash — slack that shareholder pressure cannot erode in a bull market
Personal design: leverage only below 40% of income — the household edition of dam management
Capacity planning in tech: 30% elastic headroom in AI compute and chip stock — the dam firms' share surge in the chip famine

modes.domain_zh: 商业方法论/把经营数字对内全员公开以消除猜疑并凝聚共识
modes.domain_en: Business methodology / opening the books to every employee to starve suspicion and build consensus
modes.definition_zh: 组织信任方法论/把'透明'当作治理技术而非道德姿态：松下从创业期起就把当月销售额、利润、工资发放情况公开给全体员工——'公司的事员工全知道，猜疑就没有生长的土壤'；1929 年'不裁员'决策能被全员无条件执行，前提正是十几年的玻璃式经营让员工知道公司确实到了悬崖边、也知道决策过程；他甚至把'公司为什么赚/亏'讲成全员课程——透明不仅给数据，还给因果解释；玻璃式经营的边界他也守得住：对外竞争信息严格保密，'玻璃'只朝内——透明是给同一命运共同体的信任技术，不是给对手的情报义务
modes.definition_en: Organisational-trust methodology: treat transparency as governance technology, not moral posture: from the founding years Matsushita published each month's sales, profit and payroll to all employees — 'when the staff know everything the company knows, suspicion has no soil'; the 1929 no-layoff order could be executed unconditionally because a dozen years of glass-wall management had shown employees the company truly stood at the cliff and let them see how the decision was made; he even taught 'why the firm profits or loses' as an all-staff course — transparency gives the data and the causal story; and he held its boundary firm: competitive information stayed sealed, the glass faced inward — transparency is a trust technology for one community of fate, not an intelligence duty to rivals
modes.source_chapter: 松下幸之助《玻璃式经营》(PHP 刊行)；早期'朝礼'演说记录
modes.key_quote_zh: 账本做成玻璃的——员工看得见数字，才看得见前途；猜疑只长在不透明的地方。
modes.key_quote_en: Make the ledger of glass — only when the staff can see the numbers can they see the future; suspicion grows only where there is no light.
key_concepts: 全员账本 the all-staff ledger（销售额/利润/工资按时公开——把公司变成共同事实）
因果透明 causal transparency（不只给数字，还解释为什么——数字背后的经营逻辑全员可读）
朝内玻璃 the inward glass（对内透明与对外保密的边界同样清晰）
process_zh: 确定透明清单：哪些数字对全员开放（销售额、利润、工资、经营方针）——先开放'员工利益攸关'的部分
建立固定的公开仪式：朝礼、月报、经营说明会——透明按节律发生而非按老板心情
配上因果解释：每个数字旁边说明它为什么这样——把员工从'数字旁观者'变成'逻辑共享者'
划定玻璃的边界并言明：对外竞争信息保密的原因向员工说明——边界本身也要透明
process_en: Fix the transparency list: which numbers open to all (sales, profit, payroll, policy) — open first what touches employees' own interests
Institute a fixed rhythm of disclosure: morning assemblies, monthly reports, business briefings — transparency on schedule, not on the boss's mood
Attach causal accounts: beside every number, why it is so — turning employees from spectators of figures into sharers of logic
Draw and declare the glass's boundary: explain to staff why external competitive information stays sealed — the boundary itself must be transparent
representative_cases_zh: 创业期'朝礼'：每天早上向全体员工报告前日销售与当日计划——十几人的小作坊养成了上市公司级的透明习惯
1929 年'不裁员'的执行前提：员工因常年看得见账本，相信'公司确实没钱了'，才接受'半天工+全员销售'而非怀疑资方借机压价
战后工会请愿 (1946)：驻军要整肃松下时，工会反过来联名保会长——玻璃式经营积累的信任在组织生死关头兑现
representative_cases_en: The morning assembly of the founding years: daily report of yesterday's sales and today's plan to the whole staff — a ten-man workshop cultivating listed-company-grade transparency habits

The premise of the 1929 no-layoff order: staff who had read the ledger for years believed 'the company truly has no money', accepting half-day work and all-hands selling instead of suspecting a wage squeeze
The union petition of 1946: when the Occupation moved to purge Matsushita, the union petitioned to keep the chairman — glass-wall trust cashed in at the organisation's life-or-death moment
modern_applications_zh: 创业公司全员工资透明化：Buffer 式公开薪资表——猜疑从'老板到底赚多少'消失
上市公司内部经营开放日：把月度经营数据对全员可视化——数字化时代的朝礼
危机沟通：裁员前先公开现金流与决策过程——玻璃式经营是裁员成本的减震器
modern_applications_en: Startup-wide pay transparency: Buffer-style public salary tables — the question 'what does the boss really make' simply disappears
Internal open-books days in listed firms: monthly operating data visualised to all staff — the morning assembly, digital edition
Crisis communication: publish cash flow and the decision process before any layoff — glass-wall management as the shock absorber of restructuring

modes.domain_zh: 商业方法论/把公司拆成独立核算的'社中之社'以养成经营者并压缩决策半径
modes.domain_en: Business methodology / splitting the firm into independently accounted 'companies within the company' to breed managers and shrink decision radius
modes.definition_zh: 组织设计方法论/当公司规模使'老板看不见一线、员工做不了决定'时，把公司按产品线拆成各自独立核算的事业部——每个部长对自己的工厂、销售、盈亏全权负责，总部只管资金与战略：松下 1933 年首创事业部制（比通用汽车的分权改革在日本广泛传播早得多），理由不是效率而是人：'独当一面的经营者只能在独当一面的岗位上长出来'——事业部是经营者的养成所，盈亏自负使每个部长必须自己算账、自己下注；同时事业部制压缩决策半径，收音机的事不必等电热器的事一起决定；它与玻璃式经营互为表里：分权之后账目透明才可核算，核算透明分权才不放任
modes.definition_en: Organisational-design methodology: when scale makes the boss blind to the front line and employees unable to decide, split the firm by product line into independent, separately accounted divisions — each chief owning his plant, sales, and profit-and-loss, headquarters keeping only capital and strategy: Matsushita created the divisional system in 1933 (long before GM-style decentralisation became fashionable in Japan), and his reason was not efficiency but people: 'a manager who can stand on his own grows only in a post where he must stand on his own' — divisions are academies of managers, and own-account P&L forces every chief to do his own sums and place his own bets; the system also shrinks the decision radius, so the radio's business need not wait on the heater's; it and glass-wall management are two faces of one coin: after decentralisation only open books make accounting possible, and only open accounting keeps decentralisation from becoming neglect
modes.source_chapter: 松下电器事业部制规章 (1933)；《工作·生活·思考》'事业部制的真髓'章
modes.key_quote_zh: 把公司分成一个个小公司——让部长像老板一样睡觉前算自己的账，经营者的骨头才能长硬。
modes.key_quote_en: Split the company into companies — let each chief, like an owner, do his own sums before sleep; only so do managers' bones grow hard.
key_concepts: 社中之社 company within company（独立核算的完整业务单元——盈亏自负）
经营者养成所 the manager academy（决策权与盈亏同岗——人才在压力位上长出来）
总部双权 the two总部 powers（资金调度与战略方向上收，日常经营全放）
process_zh: 按'能独立面对客户'的边界切分事业部：产品线而非职能——每个事业部都有完整的生产与销售
把核算权与用人权一起下放：部长自定预算、自聘人员、自负盈亏——总部只收资金池与战略否决权
建立事业部的内部市场规则：内部交易按市价结算、资金使用计息——防止'社中之社'变成内部垄断
按事业部业绩轮换与晋升：经营得好的部长接更大的盘子——把事业部做成经营者的梯队跑道
process_en: Draw divisional boundaries where a unit can face customers alone: product lines, not functions — each division owns its production and sales end to end
Delegate accounting and hiring together: chiefs set budgets, recruit, and carry their own P&L — headquarters keeps the capital pool and a strategic veto
Set internal-market rules: intra-group trades settle at market prices, borrowed capital accrues interest — so 'companies within the company' do not become internal monopolies
Rotate and promote by divisional results: successful chiefs take bigger scopes — the division ladder as the manager track
representative_cases_zh: 1933 年三事业部改革：收音机、电灯电池、配线器具各设事业部长独立核算——随后十年松下产品线扩张至数十种而决策半径不变
战后的'事业部群'结构：洗衣机、电视、冰箱各自事业部独立开发竞争三种神器市场——内部赛马使松下的电器普及速度领先同业
山下俊彦改革 (1977)：由空调事业部出身的非嫡系接任社长——事业部制养成的职业经理人体系完成最高一级验证
representative_cases_en: The 1933 three-division reform: radio, lamp-battery, and wiring each with its own chief and own account — as the product line spread to dozens of items over the next decade, the decision radius stayed fixed

The post-war 'divisional swarm': washing machines, televisions, refrigerators developed in competing divisions for the three-treasures market — internal horse-racing put Matsushita ahead of the industry in electrifying homes
The Yamashita reform (1977): a non-lineage chief from the air-conditioner division becoming president — the professional-manager system bred by divisions passing its highest test
modern_applications_zh: 大厂 BU 化改革：把产品线拆成独立核算 BU 并以内部计价结算（腾讯/阿里历次组织变革的底层逻辑）
创业公司避免'中心化瓶颈'：按客户群拆小分队各自背 P&L——决策半径与管理层人数解耦
家族企业传承：把事业部做成'继承者训练场'——先管好一个小盘子再接大盘子
modern_applications_en: Big-tech BU reform: product lines split into separately accounted business units with internal transfer pricing (the logic beneath Tencent's and Alibaba's reorganisations)
Escaping central bottlenecks in startups: pods split by customer group, each carrying P&L — decision radius decoupled from headcount of managers
Family-business succession: divisions as heir training grounds — run a small scope first, take the big one later

modes.domain_zh: 商业方法论/以脱产封闭、只听不辩的场域把冲突方的怨气转化为系统改革
modes.domain_en: Business methodology / converting conflict parties' grievances into systemic reform through an offsite where one listens and does not defend
modes.definition_zh: 冲突治理方法论/当渠道、客户或组织对公司的怨气积累到'开会只会互相指责'时，不在日常场合辩解，而是造一个'只解决倾听'的场：1964 年 7 月，松下代理店对厂家的积怨（强制压货、价格无人维护、返点抠门）爆发，松下把 200 多家代理店代表拉到热海的旅馆封闭三天，宣布规则：'这三天我只听，不反驳，不推销'；他听完后第三天只说了一句话'诸位说的都是对的'，然后提出全面改革销售体制的方案——倾听本身成为改革的合法性来源：因为厂家先承认了对方的一切，对方才接受了厂家的改革；这套'脱产+封闭+先听后说+当场认账+立即改革'的流程，是组织冲突处置的完整方法论
modes.definition_en: Conflict-governance methodology: when a channel's, customers' or an organisation's grievances have built to where meetings only trade accusations, do not defend in the daily venue — build a venue devoted solely to listening: in July 1964, as dealers' resentments toward the manufacturer (forced stock, unpolicced prices, stingy rebates) detonated, Matsushita took 200-plus dealer representatives to a hotel at Atami for three sealed days and set the rule: 'these three days I only listen — no rebuttal, no selling'; after two days he said only, on the third, one sentence — 'everything you say is right' — and then tabled a full reform of the sales system; the listening itself became the reform's legitimacy: because the manufacturer conceded everything first, the counterpart accepted the manufacturer's reform; offsite + sealed + listen-before-speak + concede on the spot + reform at once — a complete methodology for organisational conflict
modes.source_chapter: 热海会议 (1964 年 7 月，热海王子饭店) 与《销售体制大改革》方案；与会代理店回忆
modes.key_quote_zh: 这三天我不推销任何东西，只听——把怨气说完，生意才有地方放。
modes.key_quote_en: For these three days I will sell nothing and only listen — let the grievances finish speaking, and then business has somewhere to go.
key_concepts: 脱产场域 the offsite（离开日常权力现场——怨气需要一个没有裁判席的房间）
只听不辩 listen without defence（把'想反驳的我'请出场——倾听被制度保护）
先认全对 concede first（'都对'不是投降，是购买改革合法性的对价）
process_zh: 选场地定规则：脱离日常办公地、封闭数日、明确'只听不辩'——把倾听从姿态升级为规则
让各方把话说完：记录全部指控不给'但是'——会议的时间预算完全向倾听倾斜
当场认账并归因：先承认对方说的都对（差异只在细节），再解释成因——认账先于方案
以改革方案收尾而非补偿收尾：给出的是体制性改动（销售公司化、价格维护、返点改革）而非安抚性让步
process_en: Choose the venue and set the rule: away from the daily power site, sealed for days, 'listening only' declared — listening upgraded from posture to rule
Let every side finish: record all charges with no 'but' — the meeting's time budget tilts wholly toward hearing
Concede on the spot and attribute: affirm first that the counterpart is right (the differences being detail), then explain causes — concession before proposal
Close with reform, not compensation: deliver systemic change (sales corporatisation, price policing, rebate reform), not soothing concessions
representative_cases_zh: 热海会议 (1964)：三天倾听+一句'都对'+《销售体制大改革》——松下与代理店的信任重建，为 1965 年后的高速扩张铺平渠道
战后劳资谈判：驻军整肃时期他与工会代表的多次对谈同样采取'先听后说'——1.5 万人请愿的信任不是谈判谈出来的，是多年倾听攒出来的
PHP 研究所的'素直研究会'：把这套方法对内制度化——研究员与管理者定期封闭研讨，规则同为'先听后判'
representative_cases_en: The Atami conference (1964): three days of listening, one sentence of concession, and the Grand Reform of the Sales System — dealer trust rebuilt, paving the channel for the high-speed expansion after 1965

Post-war labour talks: his many sessions with union delegates during the purge years ran on the same listen-first rule — the 15,000-name petition was not negotiated but accumulated through years of listening
PHP's 'sunao study groups': the method institutionalised inside — researchers and managers meet in sealed retreats under the same rule, hear first and judge last
modern_applications_zh: 大客户危机处置：客户暴怒时先约'闭门倾听会'——把投诉会开成改革启动会
组织变革前的怨气清仓：并购整合前先办'只听不辩'专场——被收购方情绪处理完再谈整合
社区治理/用户运营：'AMAvsQ&A'——先公开展认全部质疑再回应，合法性完全不同
modern_applications_en: Key-account crisis: when a client erupts, book a closed listening session — turn the complaint meeting into the reform kick-off
Grievance clearance before reorganisation: before merger integration, run listen-only sessions — settle the acquired side's emotions before the integration talk
Community and user operations: AMA versus Q&A — acknowledging every question in public before answering buys legitimacy no script can

modes.domain_zh: 商业方法论/由消费者承受力倒推售价再倒逼成本，而非由成本加成定价
modes.domain_en: Business methodology / derive the price from what consumers can bear and force cost backward, instead of cost-plus pricing
modes.definition_zh: 定价方法论/把定价的因果链倒过来：不是'成本+利润=价格'，而是'消费者愿意付的价-必要利润=允许成本'，成本成为价格确定后必须被管理压到位的对象——'价格由消费者决定，成本是经营者的事'；1927 年电熨斗项目是范式：松下先定'普通主妇买得起'的价格（低于市场行情），再设计产品与工艺使成本落进这个价——电熨斗月产上万台后成本真的降到位；这与瓦特式'发明标准单位为效率定价'恰好构成定价的两极：一个让度量成为货币，一个让承受力成为货币；其推论是定价权与成本管理权必须握在同一只手里——把定价权交给市场、成本留给制造，是需求定价的完整闭环
modes.definition_en: Pricing methodology: reverse the causal chain — not 'cost plus profit equals price' but 'what the consumer will pay, minus necessary profit, equals the allowed cost', and cost becomes the object that management must force into place after the price is set: 'price is set by the consumer; cost is the manager's business'; the 1927 iron project is the paradigm: Matsushita fixed first the price an ordinary housewife could pay (below market), then designed product and process until cost fell inside it — after ten thousand irons a month, it did; against Watt's 'invent a standard unit and price by efficiency' it forms the two poles of pricing: one makes measurement the currency, the other makes affordability the currency; its corollary: pricing power and cost management must sit in the same hands — price belongs to the market, cost to manufacturing, and demand-first pricing closes the loop
modes.source_chapter: 松下幸之助《经营须知》'价格由消费者决定'条；超级电熨斗项目 (1927) 记录
modes.key_quote_zh: 先问主妇肯掏多少钱，再回去造熨斗——价格是大家的，成本是我的。
modes.key_quote_en: Ask first what the housewife will pay, then go build the iron — the price belongs to everyone; the cost is mine.
key_concepts: 价格先行 price first（承受力定价而非成本加成——因果链倒置）
允许成本 the allowed cost（售价减必要利润——成本成为被管理的目标值）
量产摊薄 volume dilution（用规模把成本压进允许成本——定价的信用靠兑现维持）
process_zh: 测定目标客群的承受力：'普通家庭为这件事愿意付多少'——用情结名义价格而非竞品价格做锚
由承受价倒推允许成本：承受价-必要利润=允许成本，写进产品立项书作为硬约束
以工艺与规模把实际成本逼进允许成本：标准化、自动化、批量采购——做不到就改设计而非改价格
以兑现建立价格信用：承诺的低价长期兑现——'松下的东西便宜且不降质'成为品牌资产
process_en: Measure the target group's affordability: 'what would an ordinary family pay for this' — anchor on the felt price, not competitors' list prices
Derive the allowed cost from the affordable price: affordable price minus necessary profit equals allowed cost, written into the project brief as a hard constraint
Force actual cost inside the allowed cost by process and scale: standardisation, automation, bulk buying — if it won't fit, change the design, not the price
Build pricing credibility by delivery: the promised low price holds for years — 'Matsushita goods are cheap and do not cheapen' becomes brand equity
representative_cases_zh: 超级电熨斗 (1927)：先定'主妇买得起'的价格再设计——月产破万台后单位成本如约下落，电熨斗从奢侈品变日用品
square 电热器与自行车灯的定价：同样以'人人用得起'为锚——低定价倒逼设计简素化与通用件化
战后黑白电视普及定价：以'何时进普通家庭'倒排价格路径——与三洋等同业在'一亿总中流'时代共同把电器价格曲线压向大众
representative_cases_en: The Super Iron (1927): fix the price the housewife can pay, then design — at ten thousand units a month unit cost fell on schedule, and the iron crossed from luxury to daily good
Pricing of the square heater and bicycle lamp: anchored likewise on 'within everyone's reach' — low prices forcing spare design and common parts

Post-war black-and-white TV pricing: the price path planned backwards from 'when it enters ordinary homes' — with peers like Sanyo pressing the appliance price curve toward the mass public in the era of the '100-million middle class'
modern_applications_zh: 硬件创业定价：先定'目标人群心理价位'再倒推 BOM——小米/大疆的立项书都写着允许成本
SaaS 分层定价：按客户规模段定价而非按服务器成本定价——承受力定价的订阅版
反向成本管理：定价公布后把'成本差距'变成全公司 OKR——价格信用倒逼组织效率
modern_applications_en: Hardware startup pricing: fix the target group's mental price, then derive the BOM — Xiaomi's and DJI's briefs carry an allowed-cost line
SaaS tiering: price by customer size band, not server cost — subscription edition of affordability pricing
Reverse cost management: once the price is public, the cost gap becomes a company-wide OKR — price credibility forcing organisational efficiency

modes.domain_zh: 成长方法论/创始人在巅峰期主动交权给制度与职业经理人而非恋栈到老
modes.domain_en: Growth methodology / the founder ceding power to institutions and professional managers at his peak instead of clinging to the chair for life
modes.definition_zh: 组织传承方法论/把'交棒'当成一项要在自己最强时做的工程，而非临终遗言：松下 1961 年 66 岁、公司正处战后增长巅峰时宣布辞去社长改任会长——'趁着身体好、判断力在，把经营交给下一代，我退到半步之外看着'；他的交棒是三层设计：人（交给你验证过的经营者而非血亲——1977 年更越过嫡系传给非松下系的山下俊彦）、制（事业部制+会长对哲学的否决权——交的是制度不是职位）、神（经营哲学成文传承——PHP 文本与社训）；对照多数家族企业的'病榻交棒'，提前交棒把继承危机的赌注从'遗嘱有效性'变成'制度成熟度'——最高权力在创建者清醒时完成第一次移交
modes.definition_en: Succession methodology: treat handover as engineering to be done at one's strongest, not a deathbed will: in 1961, at sixty-six, with the company at its post-war peak, Matsushita resigned the presidency for the chairman's seat — 'while my health and judgment last, hand operations to the next generation and I step half a pace back to watch'; the handover had three layers: person (to a proven manager, not blood — in 1977 passing the non-lineage Yamashita over the family candidates), institution (divisions plus the chairman's veto on philosophy — handing a system, not a post), and spirit (the philosophy codified in PHP texts and the company creed); against the family firm's sickbed succession, early handover moves the succession gamble from 'validity of the will' to 'maturity of the institutions' — the first transfer of supreme power completed while the founder is clear-headed
modes.source_chapter: 松下幸之助 1961 年辞任社长声明与《我的做法·我的想法》；1977 年山下俊彦社长任命
modes.key_quote_zh: 趁我还看得清棋局就离席——交出去的是制度，不是位置；留在这的是哲学，不是恩宠。
modes.key_quote_en: Leave the board while I can still read it — what I hand over is a system, not a seat; what stays behind is a philosophy, not a favour.
key_concepts: 巅峰交棒 handover at peak（趁判断力未衰时移交——继承是工程不是遗言）
传贤不传子 merit over blood（1977 年山下俊彦越系接任——把'贤'写进继承规则）
哲学护航 the philosophical veto（会长保留对经营方向的哲学否决——交权不交魂）
process_zh: 选定交棒窗口：公司处于上行周期、自己判断力未衰、继任者已经过副职验证——三者同时成立才动手
先交实权再留护航：社长职位交出，保留会长对经营哲学与节奏的最终把关——放权但不放任
把经营哲学成文：社训、PHP 文本、事业部规章——使'离场后公司仍按我的道理运转'成为可能
为二次交棒立规矩：继任者同样按贤能规则更替——1977 年越嫡系传山下即是制度对创始人的胜利
process_en: Pick the window: company on the upswing, own judgment intact, successor proven in a deputy seat — act only when all three hold
Hand over real power, keep guardianship: the presidency goes; the chairman retains final review of philosophy and tempo — delegation without neglect
Codify the philosophy: the company creed, PHP texts, divisional rules — making it possible that the firm still runs on your reasoning after you leave
Rule for the second handover: successors likewise chosen by merit — the 1977 non-lineage choice of Yamashita was the institution defeating the founder's blood preference
representative_cases_zh: 1961 年辞任社长：公司巅峰期把经营全权交给继任者，自己转向 PHP 与政经塾——权力第一次移交在创建者清醒中完成
1977 年山下俊彦越系接任：越过创始人家族与元老任命非嫡系职业经理人——'传贤'原则压倒'传亲'，松下完成向职业经理人公司的转变
晚年'半步之外'监督：不干预日常经营但保留哲学否决——交棒后的十年公司增长未断，证明提前交棒的制度红利
representative_cases_en: Resigning the presidency (1961): at the company's peak, full operations handed to a successor while he turned to PHP and the school — the first transfer of power completed clear-headed
Yamashita's elevation (1977): a professional manager outside the founding family passing over kin and elders — merit written over blood, and Matsushita became a professional-manager company
Late-life supervision 'half a pace back': no daily interference, philosophy veto retained — a decade of uninterrupted growth after the handover, the institutional dividend of leaving early
modern_applications_zh: 创始人卸任设计：公司上行期宣布交棒、保留文化否决权——Bill Gates/任正非式'半退休'的先声
职业经理人梯队：副职验证制——继任者必须先在可见位置上被验证过
家族企业去血缘化：把'传贤'写进章程——提前交棒是对抗'富不过三代'的机制
modern_applications_en: Founder exit design: announce the handover in an upswing, keep a cultural veto — the forebear of Gates's and Ren Zhengfei's 'semi-retirement'
Professional-manager ladder: prove successors in visible deputy seats before the chair
De-bloodlining the family firm: write merit into the charter — early handover as the counter to 'rich to the third generation, no further'

modes.domain_zh: 成长方法论/把一生经营所得在暮年转写为公共哲学与育人制度而非留给家业
modes.domain_en: Growth methodology / in one's last decades converting a lifetime of management into public philosophy and institutions for cultivating others, not into a family estate
modes.definition_zh: 人生后半场方法论/巅峰之后的精力投向什么——松下的答案是'把经营心得变成公共品'：1946 年 51 岁创 PHP 研究所（Peace and Happiness through Prosperity——'通过物质与精神的繁荣实现和平与幸福'），把企业利润转向经营哲学研究；1979 年 84 岁创松下政经塾，自费培养政经人才，塾训是'素直之心'；晚年更捐出巨额私财设社会科学振兴财团——他给后人的不是家业而是'企业是公器'的成文哲学；与瓦特晚岁'手艺横移'不同，松下的晚岁是'私产公共化'：把毕生赚到的钱、方法论与判断力，整体转写为不姓松下的公共制度——经营的终点被定义为教育
modes.definition_en: A late-life methodology: where should post-peak energy go — Matsushita's answer was 'turn management's lessons into public goods': in 1946, at fifty-one, he founded the PHP Institute (Peace and Happiness through Prosperity), redirecting corporate profit toward the study of the philosophy of management; in 1979, at eighty-four, the Matsushita School of Government and Economics, privately funded to cultivate public talent under the crest of 'the unbiased mind'; in his last years he gave away a vast private fortune to endow social-science research — to posterity he left not an estate but a written philosophy: the enterprise is a public instrument; unlike Watt's late lateral shift of craft, Matsushita's late act was the publicising of private wealth: a lifetime's money, method and judgment rewritten wholesale into public institutions bearing no one's name — the end of management defined as education
modes.source_chapter: PHP 研究所创立宣言 (1946)；松下政经塾塾训与开塾讲话 (1979)；松下社会科学振兴财团设立趣旨书
modes.key_quote_zh: 钱赚够了，塾才开张——我留给社会的不是松下电器，是'素直之心'这四个字的用法。
modes.key_quote_en: When the money was earned, the school opened — what I leave society is not Matsushita Electric but the usage of two words: the unbiased mind.
key_concepts: 私产公共化 privatising the private（利润与私财转投公共哲学与教育）
素直塾训 the sunao crest（把核心心法变成育人制度的入学第一课）
经营的终点 education as terminus（企业家的最后一份产品是培养下一代经营者与公职者）
process_zh: 在巅峰期就立项后半生：51 岁创 PHP——后半场工程不在暮年才动工，而在主业鼎盛时同时启动
把'我最有把握的东西'提炼为可教学件：经营哲学、素直之心、公器论——从经验里炼出可传的模块
自费建制度而非捐散财：研究所、政经塾、财团——公共化以'可持续的制度'而非一次性捐赠实现
亲自执教到生命尽头：塾训由本人在开塾讲话中亲授——传承的最后一环是当面交心
process_en: Charter the second half at the peak: PHP founded at fifty-one — the late-life project starts while the main business is at full tide
Distil what you know best into teachable modules: the philosophy of management, the unbiased mind, the public-instrument thesis — refined from experience into transmissible form
Build institutions with private money, not scatter donations: institute, school, foundation — publicising through sustainable institutions, not one-off gifts
Teach in person to the end: the crest delivered by the founder himself in the school's opening address — the last link of transmission is face to face
representative_cases_zh: PHP 研究所 (1946-)：战后废墟上办'繁荣致和平'杂志与研究——八十年来 PHP 文本成为日本经营哲学的活水源
松下政经塾 (1979-)：84 岁开塾，一期仅数人、学制数年的'极度精耕'——培养了大批国会议员与地方首长，被称为'政治家的摇篮'
松下社会科学振兴财团：巨额私财转为公共研究基金——'企业是公器'以资产负债表的形式兑现
representative_cases_en: The PHP Institute (1946-): amid post-war ruins, a magazine and research house for 'prosperity toward peace' — for eighty years PHP's texts a living source of Japanese management philosophy
The Matsushita School (1979-): opened at eighty-four, a few students a year, years of cultivation — producing members of parliament and governors, called the cradle of statesmen
The Matsushita Foundation for social sciences: vast private wealth converted to public research funding — 'the enterprise is a public instrument' cashed in on the balance sheet
modern_applications_zh: 企业家的'第二份事业'设计：功成后办研究机构/学院而非单纯慈善捐赠——方法与钱一起公共化
知识资产的制度化：把个人方法论写成教材与塾训而非自传——可教学的传承比可读的传承更深
高管退休规划：'执教型退休'——退休不退出价值观生产，转向培养下一代
modern_applications_en: The founder's second enterprise: after success, research institutes and schools rather than mere charity — publicising method and money together
Institutionalising knowledge assets: write the personal methodology into curricula and crests, not memoirs — teachable transmission beats readable transmission
Executive retirement planning: 'teaching retirement' — leaving operations but not the production of values, turning to cultivating the next generation
